cause: The Chain protocol named the post-estimation operations but did not explicitly require an actual typed step or prohibit substituting a report description for the requested calculation.
impact: A real provider created a pending workflow with a categorical model and quadratic term but placed the requested joint test and stationary point only in report prose. The proposal was declined before confirmation and no workflow step executed.
lesson: Requested post-estimation quantities must be explicit workflow steps with direct model dependencies; narrative report sections never execute a calculation.

cause: The corrected Chain protocol required explicit post-estimation steps and server artifacts supplied the resulting bounded evidence.
impact: A real Provider UI run selected a raw-data node, proposed and confirmed one five-step workflow, completed categorical OLS, a joint F test, a quadratic stationary point, and report composition, then answered from the two persisted public artifacts. Focused regression completed with 174 passed and 1 skipped.
lesson: Only the server-defined post-estimation artifacts support numerical answers; the Agent must cite those artifacts rather than infer values from workflow status or prose.

cause: bounded persisted-model coefficient evidence was available to the Global Agent
impact: Global Agent answered a cross-run coefficient comparison from persisted evidence without raw-row access or execution authority.
lesson: Project-wide numerical answers require a bounded evidence reader and explicit interpretation limits, not report-file instructions.

cause: Notebook planning previously used a synchronous provider request with no attempt-scoped cancellation and replaced usable options while replanning.

evidence.ref: 78 backend passed and 1 skipped; 38 Notebook frontend passed; 22 naming passed; TypeScript passed; browser attempt cancellation returned DELETE 200 and propose 409 twice

impact: Users can cancel an active Notebook plan, retain persisted options, retry after cancellation, and prevent late responses from replacing the current view.
lesson: Cancellation must propagate through native async provider HTTP, evict request deduplication state immediately, and keep the last ready Notebook projection visible.

cause: Notebook option batches previously derived Current from render order, confirmation was detached from its option, and successful Draft preparation did not navigate to the prepared Graph node.

evidence.ref: 111 Notebook frontend tests and 11 Graph integration tests passed; TypeScript and 22 naming tests passed; built-in browser created and focused draft_f35d6956d04b441e898751d8726bae07

impact: Notebook batches are chronological with one Current batch, Review plan opens focused inline confirmation, Prepare Draft navigates to the exact Graph node, and preparation failures remain visible inline without destroying Notebook context.
lesson: A multi-step Notebook action must preserve visible context through review and failure, while successful materialization must hand off through an explicit route identity rather than an inert success card.

cause: The first formal rescope attempted to allow backend/workbench/app.py, but the development-control validator rejects backend allow paths with fewer than four path components as overly broad.

evidence.ref: devline_control.py rescope-context returned ContextPackError: allowed_paths contains a too broad boundary path

impact: The CLI rejected the request before changing the manifest or product files.
lesson: Before expanding a frozen allowlist, check the formal validator's minimum backend path depth and prefer an already-mounted narrow router plus a leaf service module.

cause: Browser acceptance found that the collapsed run rail consumed a full-height 44px strip, Restore duplicated automatic layout actions, canvas buttons had content-sized widths, the embedded browser theme signal differed from macOS, and the detail drawer inherited a light native scrollbar in dark mode.

evidence.ref: 689 related frontend tests passed; 38 backend and naming tests passed; TypeScript passed; built-in browser measured zero-width rail, five 72px controls, no chrome overlap, light native macOS resolution, and theme-colored drawer scrollbar

impact: The collapsed rail is zero-width with a bounded overlay control; the five remaining graph controls are equal width; run status occupies a separate row; localhost system mode uses a bounded native appearance projection with browser fallback; and native drawer scrollbars inherit the effective theme.
lesson: Do not reserve a full-height rail for one collapsed control, do not keep redundant recovery actions, and do not assume an embedded browser's prefers-color-scheme is identical to the local operating-system appearance.

cause: The light-theme canvas background variable used a warm chromatic near-white that rendered as beige.

evidence.ref: 13 theme tests passed; TypeScript passed; built-in browser computed root, body, and graph canvas backgrounds as oklch(1 0 0)

impact: The light-theme root, body, graph canvas, and drawer track now resolve the shared canvas background to neutral white while cards and separators retain visual hierarchy.
lesson: Use a neutral canvas background when the product requirement is white; reserve warm tones for subordinate surfaces rather than the page background.

cause: After the canvas became white, secondary cards and borders retained warm chroma and still appeared beige.

evidence.ref: 64 related frontend tests passed; TypeScript passed; built-in browser verified white canvas and cards, neutral gray secondary surfaces, and neutral separators

impact: The light-theme canvas and primary cards are neutral white; secondary and elevated surfaces use two neutral gray levels; separators, table rows, badges, and code backgrounds use matching neutral gray contrast.
lesson: A neutral light theme must define the complete surface hierarchy together so subordinate cards and borders do not reintroduce a warm cast.

cause: The full gate exposed one stale capability projection expectation, one stale Agent navigation expectation, and twenty sandbox/code-execution failures caused by sandbox_apply being denied on this macOS host.
impact: The checkpoint cannot claim a complete host gate; the initial run ended with 21 backend failures and one frontend failure.
lesson: A durable checkpoint must separate repository inconsistencies from host containment availability before it is committed.

cause: Repository-owned stale expectations were corrected and reverified; the remaining full-gate boundary is the current host rejecting sandbox-exec profile application.
impact: Checkpoint evidence is 12 backend capability tests passed, 169 frontend files and 1450 tests passed, TypeScript passed, browser UI accepted, and Darwin sandbox execution remains host-blocked rather than verified.
lesson: A source checkpoint may preserve a host-blocked containment boundary only when the limitation is explicit and no release-pass claim is made.
